subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Quantitative research and qualitative research are two approaches to psychological study.
• Quantitative research uses statistical methods to measure and analyze numerical data.
• Such an analysis of anxiety disorders might examine survey responses from thousands of patients to identify patterns in symptom frequency.
• Qualitative research focuses on understanding experiences and meanings through detailed observation.
• Such an analysis of workplace stress might involve conducting in-depth interviews with employees to explore their personal coping strategies.
prompt: The student wants to present qualitative research to an audience unfamiliar with the concept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A quantitative analysis of anxiety disorders might examine survey responses from thousands of patients to identify patterns in symptom frequency.
choices.B: An approach to psychological study, qualitative research focuses on understanding experiences and meanings through detailed observation.
choices.C: Quantitative research differs from qualitative research in that quantitative research uses statistical methods to measure numerical data.
choices.D: In-depth interviews with employees can explore their personal coping strategies for workplace stress.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence presents qualitative research to an audience unfamiliar with the concept by defining it as an approach to psychological study that focuses on understanding experiences and meanings through detailed observation.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. It provides an example of qualitative research; it doesn't present qualitative research to an audience unfamiliar with the concept.
